subject: [SparkRide] Elevated 5xx & latency in us-west2 — routing/traffic-shift request
messages:
From: Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@sparkride.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: SparkRide SRE <sre@sparkride.com>
Date: Fri, 6 Mar 2026 16:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Production errors spike — us-west2

Sean — we’re seeing a sustained spike in 5xx rates and p99 latency starting ~15:30 PST in us-west2 (us-west-2a and 2b). Error rate jumped from ~0.6% to 6.8% and median latency doubled. This is impacting our checkout flows; we have customer-visible failures.

Attached are Grafana snapshots and spans (sparkride-monitoring-snaps-20260306.zip). Our SREs noticed a correlated increase in backend connection timeouts to your endpoints and some token refresh failures. Can Redwood route traffic to another region (us-east-1) while you triage? We need an ETA on mitigation.

— Aisha
Aisha Khan
Head of Infrastructure, SparkRide

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Production errors spike — us-west2

Aisha — thanks for the quick report and attachments. I’m escalating this to our on-call infra and CS. Initial asks: can you confirm whether the failures are evenly distributed across AZs or concentrated in a single AZ? Also, are the token refresh failures tied to a specific client ID?

Internally looping marissa (CS lead) and Vivek (infra). I’ve attached our small triage checklist to speed confirmation. I’ll propose a traffic-shift to us-east-1 as a temporary mitigation if you’re OK with cross-region latency tradeoffs.

Short term plan (proposed):
- Immediate: shift 40% of traffic to us-east-1 (gradual, health-probed)
- Mid: enable warm instances in us-east and ramp KV propagation for 10m keys
- Long: full postmortem and credits if SLA hit confirmed

I’ll update in 15 mins with our findings.

Best,

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>

Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 6 Mar 2026 16:52:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: SparkRide — elevated errors in us-west2 (need exec brief)

Quick technical summary from on-call infra:
- Observed: tail latency and 5xx correlate with a brief network control-plane disruption in us-west2 (regional AZ interconnect). That caused a spike in KV cache miss rate and a subsequent burst of cold starts on our serving pools.
- Impact: autoscaler reacted by launching additional instances but warm pools lagged; many requests hit cold kernels -> high p99 and increased 502/503.
- Contributing factor: route policy had strict AZ affinity to preserve session locality — that amplified load on the surviving AZs.

Mitigation we can do within 30 minutes:
1) Temporarily relax AZ affinity for SparkRide routes and enable cross-region fallback to us-east-1 with health-probed canary (40% -> 70% over 10 minutes).
2) Enable lightweight KV prewarm for top 10k prefixes for the customer (will reduce cold misses).
3) Throttle noisy clients at edge (we have client ID from SparkRide logs).

I will start step 1 now pending Marissa sign-off; step 2 will be kicked off and I’ll post status to JIRA INF-4721. RackCloud has been notified for the network flap but we should treat this as Redwood operational impact until proven otherwise.

Vivek Kulkarni
Sr. Engineering Manager, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai
Cc: Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@sparkride.com>, SparkRide SRE <sre@sparkride.com>, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 7 Mar 2026 01:42:00 -0800
Subject: Exec brief: SparkRide latency outage (us-west2) — mitigation & asks

Quick exec summary for Rishi / Marissa / Priyom:
- Incident: Starting 15:30 PST 3/6, SparkRide observed elevated 5xx (~6.8%) and p99 latency ~2x in us-west2. Root cause: regional interconnect issue + AZ-affinity routing that increased load on surviving nodes and caused cold cache storms.
- Customer impact: degraded checkout for a subset of users (business impact flagged by SparkRide). They are asking for immediate cross-region routing.
- Actions taken: Vivek initiated cross-region canary to us-east-1 (40% traffic) and kicked KV prewarm. RackCloud engaged; on-call is monitoring.
- Current status: error rate trending down (from 6.8% to ~1.4%) after canary ramp to 55%. No data loss; token refresh errors being investigated (likely timeouts).

Asks / approvals:
1) Approve temporary credit/waiver up to $6,000 for this incident (if attribution shows Redwood systemic fault).
2) Sign-off to make the relaxed routing policy sticky for 2 hours while we stabilize.
3) Postmortem owner: Vivek (infra) + Marissa (CS) — deliverable: incident timeline + remediation in 72 hours.

Attachments: postmortem-draft.md (initial timeline)

I’ll wait for quick replies; if no objections in 20 minutes I’ll approve the routing change to full 70% and notify SparkRide.

Thanks,
Sean Gallagher
Account Exec — Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
